StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `=> false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533; the sim never removes powers on death, so `false` is its universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. The inverse -- the C# default is `true` and the sim strips nothing -- is the engine-wide absence reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

AfterAttack.issue: **re-executes the record's own two claims rather than trusting its prose.** (1) The hook fix the round-13 NARROWED note describes is confirmed still in the tree exactly as claimed: `PainfulStabsPower.after_attack` (powers.py) groups `command.Results` by player receiver, counts each receiver's unblocked-damage hits, and adds `Amount * hits` Wounds once — matching `PainfulStabsPower.cs:34-68`. Pinned by `test_painful_stabs_after_attack_fixed_shape_still_holds`. (2) The residual — `PainfulStabsPower.cs:36`'s third early-return disjunct, `!command.DamageProps.IsPoweredAttack()`, not expressed in the port — is re-confirmed DORMANT, not merely re-asserted: grepped every `DamageCmd.deal(` call under `sts2_rl/monsters/` with an explicit `props=` argument (one hit, `monsters/glory/fabricator.py`, and it is a `BlockCmd.apply` call, not damage — no monster damage call anywhere sets Unpowered), and then EXECUTED `Monster._execute_attack` (`monsters/base.py`, the sole shared attack entry point every hand-rolled and machine monster funnels through) with a `DamageCmd.deal` spy that records the actually-inferred `props` for each hit — all Move, none Unpowered (`test_no_ported_monster_attack_deals_unpowered_move_damage`). So today's owner (an enemy) can never reach an Unpowered attack, and the guard has no witness.

guards.issue: RE-OPENED 2026-07-28. Two of the three early-return conditions map; the THIRD does not, and the AfterAttack hook entry in this record already says so ("NOTE this record's guard on 'the three AfterAttack early-return conditions' still reads `faithful`, which is no longer true of the third one") -- the re-derivation pass wrote that sentence and left this entry at `faithful` anyway. PainfulStabsPower.cs:36 is `command.Attacker != base.Owner || command.TargetSide == base.Owner.Side || !command.DamageProps.IsPoweredAttack()`. The sim's after_attack bracket carries no props at all -- `def after_attack(self, dealer, card=None)` (hooks.py), which passes only (dealer, card, results) to listeners (hooks.py) -- and powers.py tests only `dealer is not self.owner` and, per result, `receiver.side != "player"`. So the IsPoweredAttack test has no expression anywhere on this path. DORMANT today (Monster._execute_attack, monsters/base.py, always brackets powered MOVE damage), and folded with the AfterAttack entry's residual: one mechanism, one verdict. CITATION FIX: the old rationale cited powers.py for the props test; after the powers.py reshuffle those lines are inside HexPower, and the code they described no longer exists at that location. The two conditions that DO map: `command.Attacker != base.Owner` -> `dealer is not self.owner`, and `command.TargetSide == base.Owner.Side` -> the per-receiver `receiver.side != "player"` filter, which is equivalent for a single-player enemy owner.
